old_problem: The historical record retained Pending and Source Conflict because the source leaves selector/value placeholders, reads only block zero and has no recovery. IPMI v2.0 sections 22.14a/b and Table 22-16c define 0x58/0x59, Set In Progress/optional commit, selectors 1-4, 16-byte set-selector blocks, encoding and total byte length. Exact test string and platform rollback support remain approved Project inputs rather than unknown core semantics.
disposition_reason: Preserve actual write coverage, both source transports and selectors 0-4 without batch mutation. For one approved selector 1-4 per run, capture every existing block and all unrelated parameters, establish Set In Progress through selector 0, write a harmless owner-approved encoded value through IB, complete/commit by the platform's documented standard state machine, verify all blocks via both paths, then use OOB to restore the exact multi-block baseline and cross-verify. Selector 0 is exercised as transaction control, not left stuck. Never guess rollback support, write multiple identity fields, clear logs or retry an uncertain transaction.
decision_basis: XLSX row 1012, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 1013 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 1013 / variant 8e5308027020bdd4.

IPMI v2.0 sections 22.14a/b define App 0x58 selector+data, 0x59 get/revision/set-selector/block-selector, parameter revision and completions 80h unsupported, 81h Set In Progress conflict and 82h read-only.
Table 22-16c defines selector 0 states: 00 complete, 01 in progress, optional 10 commit and reserved 11. The flag is notification only, not a lock; concurrent writers must be excluded operationally.

Selectors 1 System Firmware Version, 2 System Name, 3 Primary OS Name and 4 Present OS Name use zero-based 16-byte data blocks selected within parameter data. First-string metadata defines encoding 0 ASCII+Latin1, 1 UTF-8 or 2 Unicode and total byte length; all required blocks must be preserved/read.

Selectors 1-3 are non-volatile; selector 4 is volatile and automatically cleared on power cycle/reset. Parameter 1 may also be maintained by system firmware. The Project owner must choose one compatible field/value and documented persistence; selector 1 is not a safe default.

ED-02, ED-03, ED-15 through ED-19, ED-22, ED-24 and ED-26 through ED-30 preserve duplicate/transport identity, write/readback and evidence; ED-33 through ED-38 allow parameterization while forbidding placeholders, partial readback, log clear or blind retry.

test_case.test_name: Set one approved System Info string over IB, verify cross-path, and restore full baseline over OOB
test_case.purpose: Verify standard Set System Info can transactionally change exactly one approved selector through the in-band path, expose the exact encoded multi-block value through both IB/OOB reads, then restore the complete original value through the source-required OOB write without changing any unrelated System Info field or BMC health.
required_package: Immutable DUT/host/BMC/local-interface mapping, firmware identity, pinned ipmitool and protected App 0x58/0x59 state-machine encoder/decoder

Versioned selector matrix for 1-4 defining support, ownership, volatility, allowed encoding/length, exact harmless test value, expected persistence and Project-approved coverage; execute one selector per approval
Platform/OEM statement of Set In Progress rollback and optional commit behavior; do not probe commit support by an unplanned write
Complete raw baseline of selector 0 and every available block for selectors 1-4 from both paths, plus exact restore blocks and hashes; preserve padding bytes rather than regenerating them
Protected OOB recovery/restore path, independent BMC/identity/consumer observer, immediate approval, concurrent-writer exclusion and no-retry/incident runbook
test_case.test_command:
AUTHORIZED HYBRID PROCEDURE ONLY; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Bind the exact same BMC on local IB and protected OOB. Preserve logs. With raw `0x06 0x59 0x00 0x00`, enumerate and archive every required 16-byte block for selectors 1-4 and selector-0 state from both paths; use the first block's encoding/total byte length to determine the full block set and retain raw padding. Require selector 0 = complete and no concurrent writer. Select exactly one owner-approved parameter `

` in 1..4 and encode one harmless test string under Table 22-16c; never default to firmware version. Display the full baseline, all planned `0x58` block requests, rollback/commit policy and OOB restore, then obtain point-of-action confirmation. Through IB set selector 0 to in-progress with `ipmitool raw 0x06 0x58 0x00 0x01`; write each precomputed block exactly once as `raw 0x06 0x58

<16-byte-block>`. If and only if documented rollback is implemented, issue the approved optional commit state 0x02, then always return selector 0 to complete 0x00; otherwise use the documented immediate-write path and complete state. Read every block and all unrelated selectors over both IB/OOB; require only `

` equals the test value. Start a separately approved restore transaction over OOB, write every original raw block for `

`, perform the documented commit/complete sequence, and cross-read every block over both paths until the full baseline is exact. Never clear logs, leave in-progress set, write multiple selectors, infer unsupported commit, use plaintext credentials, reset/power cycle or retry after ambiguous completion.
test_case.expected_result: The pre-state is complete and identical across paths. One approved selector changes via the IB transaction to the exact encoded multi-block test value, both IB/OOB 0x59 reads decode it identically, and every unrelated parameter remains byte-identical. The OOB transaction restores every original raw block, selector 0 returns complete, both paths match the complete baseline and BMC/consumers/logs remain healthy.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact target, complete dual-path baseline, one approved selector/value, valid encoding/length/block sequence, immediate confirmation, documented Set In Progress/commit behavior, successful IB write, complete dual-path readback, no unrelated drift, successful OOB full-block restore and exact final baseline. Completion 00 alone, only block 0, placeholder bytes, concurrent state 81h, unsupported 80h, read-only 82h, selector 1 without explicit ownership, stuck in-progress, path divergence, missing padding/baseline, log clear, retry or failed restore cannot pass. Missing runtime inputs is NOT READY, not Pending; N/A requires platform SPEC proof.
safety_gate: Require point-of-action confirmation after displaying selected field, current and test strings, raw block diffs, persistence, Set In Progress/commit sequence and exact OOB restore bytes.
Execute one selector 1-4 per approval; selector 0 is only transaction control. Do not batch identity fields or use OEM selectors.
Treat Set In Progress as notification, not locking. Stop if it is not complete initially or another writer/management agent cannot be excluded.
Do not default to System Firmware Version; its ownership/auto-update semantics require explicit Project/firmware approval. Respect selector 4 volatile power/reset behavior without inducing a cycle.
Preserve logs and the full raw baseline including padding. Protect OOB secrets and maintain an independent access path until exact restore is verified.
No automatic retry after timeout or uncertain block/commit/complete result. Read state once under the approved verification plan, stop further blocks and escalate.
expected_evidence: Target/firmware/local-interface/tool/parser identity, selector matrix, rollback/commit support statement and protected OOB policy
Complete dual-path raw pre-baseline for selector 0 and every block of selectors 1-4, decoded strings/encoding/lengths and hashes
Immediate approval, exact IB in-progress/block/commit/complete requests/responses and no-retry audit
Complete dual-path post-write raw/decoded comparison proving only the selected field changed
Exact OOB restore transaction, final selector-0 complete state, full dual-path byte-for-byte baseline recovery, BMC/consumer/log health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On uncertain write/commit/complete, do not resend. Stop all new blocks, preserve raw responses, read selector 0 and the complete parameter set once through the independent approved path, then let the owner choose the single restore/complete action. If the IB test value is known committed, use the pre-approved OOB transaction to restore the exact saved blocks; if restore fails or unrelated fields drift, leave evidence intact and escalate to BMC/platform/inventory owners. Do not reset/power cycle, clear logs, rewrite other selectors or improvise padding/encoding.

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1
external_authorities.application: Sections 22.14a/b, Tables 22-16a/b/c and Appendix G define optional App 0x58/0x59, completions, Set In Progress/rollback/commit, selectors 1-4, 16-byte blocks, encodings, lengths and volatility.

project_authority: The Project BMC/inventory owner selects one safe field and exact test string, confirms field ownership/persistence and platform commit behavior, excludes concurrent writers, approves the two transport transactions and owns recovery. Project approval cannot turn placeholders, partial block reads, guessed commit support or an unrecovered identity change into PASS.
